note.explanation: A speed-time graph shows how an object's speed changes with time. The shape of the line helps us describe the motion.
examples: A straight line rising from the origin shows speed increasing by the same amount in equal time intervals.
A horizontal line shows that speed stays the same as time passes.
note.checkAnswer: A horizontal line parallel to the time axis represents constant speed.
note.simple: Look at the line: rising means speed is increasing; horizontal means speed is unchanged.
note.checkQuestion: What kind of motion is shown by a straight line rising upward on a speed-time graph when speed increases equally every second?
note.title: Reading a speed-time graph
steps: Put time t on the x-axis and speed v on the y-axis.
Mark the speed at each time.
Join the points and observe the shape of the line.
note.answer: A speed-time graph is a graph between speed v and time t. A straight line rising upward shows uniform acceleration; a horizontal line shows constant speed.

written.text: Prove that the area under speed-time graph is equal to the distance covered by an object.
written.finalAnswer: The area under a speed-time graph is equal to the distance covered by the object.

rubric.why: The proof must relate distance, speed, and time.
rubric.description: Use the relation between speed, distance, and time.
rubric.how: State that speed = distance/time, so distance = speed × time.

rubric.description: Identify the area under a constant-speed graph.
rubric.how: State that the area is the rectangle formed by the speed and time axes.

rubric.why: The rectangle's area must be connected to the distance.
rubric.description: Relate the rectangle's area to distance.

rubric.why: A changing speed can be considered over successive time intervals.
rubric.description: Extend the reasoning to changing speed.
rubric.how: Explain that the total area is the sum of areas for successive intervals.

rubric.why: The final statement must give the result being proved.
rubric.how: Conclude that the area under the speed-time graph equals the distance covered.

modelAnswer: For a body moving at constant speed, speed = distance/time.
The area under its speed-time graph is the area of a rectangle = speed × time.
Hence, the area of the rectangle is equal to the distance covered.
For changing speed, the total area under the graph is the sum of the distances covered in successive time intervals.
Therefore, the area under a speed-time graph is equal to the distance covered by the object.

explain.title: What a speed-time graph shows
explain.body: A speed-time graph represents speed v against time t. In the section's first example, time is on the x-axis and speed is on the y-axis.

explain.title: A rising straight line
explain.body: In the first table, speed increases by 8 m s⁻¹ every second. The graph is a straight line rising upward, showing motion with uniform acceleration.

explain.title: A horizontal line
explain.body: In the second table, speed remains 20 m s⁻¹ at every recorded time. Its graph is horizontal and parallel to the time axis, showing constant speed.

mistakes: Do not put speed on the x-axis and time on the y-axis; the section puts time on x and speed on y.
Do not call a horizontal speed-time line uniform acceleration: it represents constant speed.
Do not describe a rising straight line as constant speed; its speed is increasing.
When explaining uniform acceleration, mention that speed changes by the same amount in equal time intervals.
